raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation
Relate #35011

Adds native support for [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview),
SandAI's 114B MoE model that generates a video and its synchronized stereo
soundtrack in one denoising trajectory. About 6B parameters are active per token.

Audio is not a second pass over finished video: video and audio latents share one
packed sequence and one denoise loop. Text-to-video and image+text-to-video are
both supported.

The checkpoint ships two DiTs. A preview model denoises the clip, and a refiner
then takes that result to 1920x1088; the words "preview" and "refiner" below always
mean those two.

Serving it today means standing up a second stack. The reference implementation
launches under `torchrun`, depends on SandAI's own kernels
([MagiAttention](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiAttention),
[MagiCompiler](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiCompiler), FlashAttention 3) and so
ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview), and its
checkpoint has no `model_index.json`. This PR builds it against SGLang's own layers
so it is served like every other family in `sglang.multimodal_gen`.

## Modifications

### New code

Four pieces the tree did not already have. Everything else goes through existing
machinery.

- **Multi-head MoE** (`runtime/layers/moe_multihead.py`). MAGI-2 routes 12
  independent heads over 256 experts each, top-6, where the tree's MoE assumes one
  routing head. Viewing tokens as `[N * 12, 256]` instead of `[N, 12, 256]` makes it
  a standard MoE with `hidden_size=256` and `num_experts=3072`, so srt's Triton
  `fused_experts` runs unmodified. A rank owns `(12 / ep_size) * 256` of those, and
  `moe_align_block_size` runs 1024 threads while indexing `prefix[num_experts]`, so
  anything past 1023 takes an illegal memory access; the experts run in balanced head
  chunks that fit, which is one call at `ep_size >= 4` and is what lets 1, 2 and 3
  work at all. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU
  approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and
  `gemm1_clamp_limit`.
- **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs
  use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend
  accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed
  through, along with `window_size`.
- **Block-window local attention**
  (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer
  restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent
  block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as
  a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through
  `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. The same mask is also expressed as
  token-range pairs for MagiAttention's `flex_flash_attn_func`, which is used when
  that package is importable and is 1.78x faster on the refiner's shape; without it
  the `flex_attention` path runs unchanged.
- **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The
  preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288,
  mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly
  stochastic.

### Reused from the tree

Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them:

- **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded
  once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get
  their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them.
- **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the
  same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. `ep_size` defaults to the world size and
  can be set below it through `--pipeline-config-path`, which is how 8 ranks run.
- **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and
  `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work
  without model-specific code.
- `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC
  scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the
  `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts.

### Structure

Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`.
Two orderings matter and are easy to break in review:

Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs
a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs
**after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the
clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis,
and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding.

The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because
video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler
state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile,
residency and warmup still come from the base stage.

### Parallelism

`--num-gpus` must divide every Ulysses head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on
all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA
key/value heads. The preview's 12 MoE heads are sharded by `ep_size` instead and are
checked against that. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2, 4 or 8
and preview-only also admits 3, 6 and 12. All four axes are checked in
`validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a
collective.

8 GPUs divides every Ulysses axis but not the preview's 12 MoE heads, so it needs an
explicit `ep_size` of 4: two expert-parallel groups of 4 ranks, each holding all 12
heads. The reference instead pads the head axis to 16 and gives the spare ranks
zero-weight experts; this PR needs no padding and leaves no rank idle.

`--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches
itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance.

Expert parallelism is also what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them
fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while
the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. Below 4 ranks the expert weights need
`--dit-layerwise-offload` to fit at all.

### Deliberate divergences from the reference

Both are marked at the site in the code.

**The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it
at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly
doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length, which
the two-stage tier does not have to spare. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores
in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the
rotary.

**Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, and is not needed: an `ep_size`
below the world size reaches 8 ranks without it, as described under Parallelism.

### Docs

`docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism
rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility
matrix.

### Known limitations

- Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise.
  1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16.
- 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration.
- `--enable-torch-compile` must be paired with `--regional-compile`. On its own it
  compiles the whole transformer, and inductor autotuning then fails on the
  multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has
  (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`). With `--regional-compile`
  the expert GEMMs stay out of the compiled region and both DiTs compile per block.
  Compile is also rank-count dependent: it pays at 4 ranks and loses at 8, where the
  preview pass measures 335s compiled against 184s eager.
- 1 GPU passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview DiT, which
  casts the whole state dict to the device before layerwise offload can take over.
- 2 GPUs needs `--dit-layerwise-offload`; the expert weights are 217 GB.
- `ep_size` has no CLI flag, so the 8-rank launch needs
  `--pipeline-config-path` with `{"ep_size": 4}`.
- `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below.
- FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so
  `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded.
- The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its
  decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise
  tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is
  unset.

## Accuracy Tests

### Side-by-side with the reference implementation

Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same
seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference
implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own
long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording.

**Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second
Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest
into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the
climax.

- Reference: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a

- This PR: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67

**Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the
conditioning image.

- Reference: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51

- This PR: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d


**Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay
animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at
his feet — plus its conditioning still.

- Reference:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 

- This PR: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964


The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. This PR runs SGLang's own
attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates
the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate
divergences. The clips are the thing to look at.

### Prompt coverage

Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static
and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English:

- Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe


- Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20


- Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38


- Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc


- Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e


- 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9


- Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b



- Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling —

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23



All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps,
249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than
being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the
lake clip is continuous and low-frequency.

### Unit tests

59 unit tests, 51 of which need no GPU: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC
normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder,
packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance
arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in,
sequence bucketing, the expert-axis sharding predicate, and which submodules the
regional-compile conditions select. The remaining 8 need CUDA and are skipped
without it: the mHC mixing kernel against an FP32 reference, and the block-window
mask against a dense `scaled_dot_product_attention` reference.

They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up
and they run in the existing suite with no CI change:

```
python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit
```

The full 1080p path needs at least two cards and minutes per clip, so it is not in
the suite.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with
`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative
comparisons, not as sizing targets. They are eager-mode figures; the compiled
configuration and the comparison against the reference are in Benchmark below.

**One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:**
text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under
0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once
per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the
conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to
encode — and measures 741s.

**Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave
refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat,
which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on
the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in
the host page cache.

**Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses
124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using
more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer,
so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those
ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup
rather than left for a user to discover.

**Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text +
reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is
compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where
the first three share a prompt length:

- rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s
- using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory

Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up
to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt
range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the
valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, since dynamo guards a captured int
by value and would recompile per prompt length even at a fixed shape. `dynamic=True`
is not an alternative; it costs 26s per clip.

## Benchmark

Same box, same weights, same seed 42, same 1920x1088 two-stage tier at 100 preview +
5 refiner steps, 4 ranks on each side. This PR runs `--enable-torch-compile
--regional-compile`. Nine clips per side, discarding each process's first clip while
its graphs are still building.

One clip is 249 frames at 25 fps — just under 10 seconds of 1920x1088 video with its
synchronized stereo audio, generated together in one denoising trajectory. 10 seconds
is the only duration the model was trained for, so the figures below do not scale with
a requested length. Weight loading is separate and paid once per process, about 5
minutes for both DiTs.

| | reference | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| preview denoise (100 steps) | 277.7s | 286.6s |
| refiner denoise (5 steps) | 46.1s | 41.9s |
| decode (video and audio) | 8.9s | 7.8s |
| **one clip, end to end** | **344.9s** | **349.3s** |

**At 4 ranks this PR is 1.3% slower** — 4.4s on a 345s clip, which is larger than the
spread between runs. The refiner and the decode are faster; preview denoise is 8.9s
slower and is where the difference sits. Stage times do not sum to the end-to-end row
on either side, because the two implementations synchronize at different points, so the
end-to-end row is the one to compare.

### Across topologies

Same clip, same seed, each column at that rank count's best configuration. Two steady
clips per arm on one 8-GPU box, so this is a narrower measurement than the nine-clip
table above; the 4-rank column reproduces its 349.3s within the noise floor, which is
what makes the columns comparable:

| | 2 ranks | 4 ranks | 8 ranks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ep_size` | 2 | 4 (default) | 4 |
| compile | regional | regional | **none** |
| offload | layerwise | none | none |
| preview denoise (100 steps) | 590.4s | 286.9s | 183.9s |
| refiner denoise (5 steps) | 79.4s | 41.3s | 31.6s |
| decode (video and audio) | 7.1s | 8.8s | 12.2s |
| **one clip, end to end** | **689.0s** | **348.2s** | **253.5s** |
| peak memory | 132208 MiB | 85274 MiB | 126572 MiB |
| GPU-seconds per clip | 1378 | 1393 | 2028 |

8 ranks is 1.37x faster per clip and spends 46% more GPU-time to get there, so it buys
latency rather than throughput, and two concurrent 4-rank deployments beat one 8-rank
deployment on total output. 2 and 4 ranks cost the same GPU-seconds, so the 2-rank arm
trades latency for hardware at no efficiency loss. Decode moves the wrong way with rank
count, so every latency gain comes from denoise.

The 8-rank arm runs eager deliberately: compiled, its preview pass measures 335.4s
against 183.9s, which is the only configuration in this PR where `--regional-compile`
is a loss. 1 rank passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview
DiT. The reference was not re-run at 8 ranks, so none of these are head-to-head; its
published 8-rank timings use head padding and a different step budget.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

  `moe_align_block_size` runs 1024 threads while indexing `prefix[num_experts]`, so
  anything past 1023 takes an illegal memory access; the experts run in balanced head
  chunks that fit, which is one call at `ep_size >= 4` and is what lets 1, 2 and 3
  work at all. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU
  approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and
  `gemm1_clamp_limit`.
- **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs
  use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend
  accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed
  through, along with `window_size`.
- **Block-window local attention**
  (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer
  restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent
  block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as
  a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through
  `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. The same mask is also expressed as
  token-range pairs for MagiAttention's `flex_flash_attn_func`, which is used when
  that package is importable and is 1.78x faster on the refiner's shape; without it
  the `flex_attention` path runs unchanged.
- **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The
  preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288,
  mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly
  stochastic.

### Reused from the tree

Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them:

- **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded
  once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get
  their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them.
- **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the
  same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. `ep_size` defaults to the world size and
  can be set below it through `--pipeline-config-path`, which is how 8 ranks run.
- **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and
  `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work
  without model-specific code.
- `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC
  scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the
  `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts.

### Structure

Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`.
Two orderings matter and are easy to break in review:

Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs
a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs
**after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the
clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis,
and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding.

The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because
video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler
state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile,
residency and warmup still come from the base stage.

### Parallelism

`--num-gpus` must divide every Ulysses head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on
all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA
key/value heads. The preview's 12 MoE heads are sharded by `ep_size` instead and are
checked against that. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2, 4 or 8
and preview-only also admits 3, 6 and 12. All four axes are checked in
`validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a
collective.

8 GPUs divides every Ulysses axis but not the preview's 12 MoE heads, so it needs an
explicit `ep_size` of 4: two expert-parallel groups of 4 ranks, each holding all 12
heads. The reference instead pads the head axis to 16 and gives the spare ranks
zero-weight experts; this PR needs no padding and leaves no rank idle.

`--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches
itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance.

Expert parallelism is also what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them
fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while
the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. Below 4 ranks the expert weights need
`--dit-layerwise-offload` to fit at all.

### Deliberate divergences from the reference

Both are marked at the site in the code.

**The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it
at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly
doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length, which
the two-stage tier does not have to spare. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores
in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the
rotary.

**Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, and is not needed: an `ep_size`
below the world size reaches 8 ranks without it, as described under Parallelism.

### Docs

`docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism
rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility
matrix.

### Known limitations

- Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise.
  1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16.
- 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration.
- `--enable-torch-compile` must be paired with `--regional-compile`. On its own it
  compiles the whole transformer, and inductor autotuning then fails on the
  multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has
  (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`). With `--regional-compile`
  the expert GEMMs stay out of the compiled region and both DiTs compile per block.
  Compile is also rank-count dependent: it pays at 4 ranks and loses at 8, where the
  preview pass measures 335s compiled against 184s eager.
- 1 GPU passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview DiT, which
  casts the whole state dict to the device before layerwise offload can take over.
- 2 GPUs needs `--dit-layerwise-offload`; the expert weights are 217 GB.
- `ep_size` has no CLI flag, so the 8-rank launch needs
  `--pipeline-config-path` with `{"ep_size": 4}`.
- `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below.
- FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so
  `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded.
- The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its
  decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise
  tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is
  unset.

## Accuracy Tests

### Side-by-side with the reference implementation

Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same
seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference
implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own
long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording.

**Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second
Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest
into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the
climax.

- Reference: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a

- This PR: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67

**Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the
conditioning image.

- Reference: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51

- This PR: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d


**Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay
animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at
his feet — plus its conditioning still.

- Reference:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 

- This PR: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964


The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. This PR runs SGLang's own
attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates
the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate
divergences. The clips are the thing to look at.

### Prompt coverage

Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static
and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English:

- Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe


- Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20


- Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38


- Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc


- Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e


- 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9


- Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b



- Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling —

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23



All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps,
249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than
being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the
lake clip is continuous and low-frequency.

### Unit tests

59 unit tests, 51 of which need no GPU: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC
normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder,
packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance
arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in,
sequence bucketing, the expert-axis sharding predicate, and which submodules the
regional-compile conditions select. The remaining 8 need CUDA and are skipped
without it: the mHC mixing kernel against an FP32 reference, and the block-window
mask against a dense `scaled_dot_product_attention` reference.

They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up
and they run in the existing suite with no CI change:

```
python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit
```

The full 1080p path needs at least two cards and minutes per clip, so it is not in
the suite.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with
`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative
comparisons, not as sizing targets. They are eager-mode figures; the compiled
configuration and the comparison against the reference are in Benchmark below.

**One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:**
text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under
0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once
per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the
conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to
encode — and measures 741s.

**Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave
refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat,
which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on
the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in
the host page cache.

**Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses
124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using
more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer,
so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those
ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup
rather than left for a user to discover.

**Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text +
reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is
compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where
the first three share a prompt length:

- rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s
- using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory

Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up
to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt
range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the
valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, since dynamo guards a captured int
by value and would recompile per prompt length even at a fixed shape. `dynamic=True`
is not an alternative; it costs 26s per clip.

## Benchmark

Same box, same weights, same seed 42, same 1920x1088 two-stage tier at 100 preview +
5 refiner steps, 4 ranks on each side. This PR runs `--enable-torch-compile
--regional-compile`. Nine clips per side, discarding each process's first clip while
its graphs are still building.

One clip is 249 frames at 25 fps — just under 10 seconds of 1920x1088 video with its
synchronized stereo audio, generated together in one denoising trajectory. 10 seconds
is the only duration the model was trained for, so the figures below do not scale with
a requested length. Weight loading is separate and paid once per process, about 5
minutes for both DiTs.

| | reference | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| preview denoise (100 steps) | 277.7s | 286.6s |
| refiner denoise (5 steps) | 46.1s | 41.9s |
| decode (video and audio) | 8.9s | 7.8s |
| **one clip, end to end** | **344.9s** | **349.3s** |

**At 4 ranks this PR is 1.3% slower** — 4.4s on a 345s clip, which is larger than the
spread between runs. The refiner and the decode are faster; preview denoise is 8.9s
slower and is where the difference sits. Stage times do not sum to the end-to-end row
on either side, because the two implementations synchronize at different points, so the
end-to-end row is the one to compare.

### Across topologies

Same clip, same seed, each column at that rank count's best configuration. Two steady
clips per arm on one 8-GPU box, so this is a narrower measurement than the nine-clip
table above; the 4-rank column reproduces its 349.3s within the noise floor, which is
what makes the columns comparable:

| | 2 ranks | 4 ranks | 8 ranks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ep_size` | 2 | 4 (default) | 4 |
| compile | regional | regional | **none** |
| offload | layerwise | none | none |
| preview denoise (100 steps) | 590.4s | 286.9s | 183.9s |
| refiner denoise (5 steps) | 79.4s | 41.3s | 31.6s |
| decode (video and audio) | 7.1s | 8.8s | 12.2s |
| **one clip, end to end** | **689.0s** | **348.2s** | **253.5s** |
| peak memory | 132208 MiB | 85274 MiB | 126572 MiB |
| GPU-seconds per clip | 1378 | 1393 | 2028 |

8 ranks is 1.37x faster per clip and spends 46% more GPU-time to get there, so it buys
latency rather than throughput, and two concurrent 4-rank deployments beat one 8-rank
deployment on total output. 2 and 4 ranks cost the same GPU-seconds, so the 2-rank arm
trades latency for hardware at no efficiency loss. Decode moves the wrong way with rank
count, so every latency gain comes from denoise.

The 8-rank arm runs eager deliberately: compiled, its preview pass measures 335.4s
against 183.9s, which is the only configuration in this PR where `--regional-compile`
is a loss. 1 rank passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview
DiT. The reference was not re-run at 8 ranks, so none of these are head-to-head; its
published 8-rank timings use head padding and a different step budget.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

Ulysses spans all four ranks, and expert +parallelism defaults to that same world size, which divides the 12 MoE heads: + +```bash 4 GPUs recommended +sglang serve \ + --model-path sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview \ + --num-gpus 4 \ + --ulysses-degree 4 \ + --performance-mode speed \ + --port 30010 +``` + +`--performance-mode speed` keeps components GPU-resident for lowest latency. +Use it only after confirming the workload fits; see the offload section below +when it does not. + +Both DiTs use attention sinks and a packed variable-length attention path that +are implemented only on the FlashAttention backend. Sink logits are silently +dropped on any other backend, so MAGI-2 restricts itself to FlashAttention and +does not accept `--attention-backend sage_attn`. + +The first launch downloads the checkpoint. If the repository requires +authentication, export a Hugging Face token in the server environment. + +## 5. Generate video and audio + + + + + +Text only. The defaults already describe the two-stage 1080p tier, so a minimal +request changes nothing but the prompt and seed. + +Pass long prompts inline with `--prompt`. Do not use `--prompt-file-path` or +`--prompt-path` for a single long caption: both read a file and split it into one +request per non-empty line, which turns a wrapped paragraph into many unrelated +short prompts. + +```bash Command +sglang generate \ + --model-path sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview \ + --num-gpus 4 \ + --ulysses-degree 4 \ + --performance-mode speed \ + --prompt "A cellist tunes up alone in a wood-panelled rehearsal room at dusk, then draws one long low note; dust turns in the last of the window light and the room's natural reverb settles around the sound." \ + --seed 1101 \ + --save-output +``` + + + + + +Supply a conditioning image with `--image-path`. Prefer it over the shorter +spellings: `--image-path` and its `--image-paths` alias are the flags that +actually feed image-to-video conditioning, and several other flags begin with +`--image`. + +MAGI-2 VAE-encodes the original conditioning image rather than a resized and +centre-cropped copy, so the generic TI2V preprocessing path is deliberately +skipped. + +```bash Command +sglang generate \ + --model-path sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview \ + --num-gpus 4 \ + --ulysses-degree 4 \ + --performance-mode speed \ + --prompt "The camera pushes in slowly on the supplied frame as steam rises from the cup and quiet kitchen sounds settle in." \ + --image-path "" \ + --seed 2101 \ + --save-output +``` + + + + + +Request the preview geometry to skip the refiner entirely. A request delivered +at the preview size leaves the refiner nothing to do, so the second pass is +skipped even when its weights are loaded: + +```bash Command +sglang generate \ + --model-path sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview \ + --num-gpus 4 \ + --ulysses-degree 4 \ + --performance-mode speed \ + --width 896 \ + --height 512 \ + --prompt "Rain moves across a quiet street at night while a single neon sign buzzes overhead." \ + --seed 3101 \ + --save-output +``` + + +`--fps` is validated as an integer, so the preview tier's 12.5 fps delivered +rate cannot be named exactly on the command line. Leave `--num-frames` and +`--fps` at their defaults and select the tier through `--width`/`--height` +alone. + + + + + + +To skip loading the refiner weights altogether rather than skipping the pass, +turn the refiner off in the pipeline configuration. There is no CLI flag for it; +see the configuration notes below. + +## 6. Offload + +The preview DiT's expert weights are the memory driver. There are 256 experts +per head across 12 heads in each of 36 MoE layers, and they dominate resident +footprint even though only 6 experts per head are active for a given token. When +a topology cannot hold them, offload the DiT rather than shrinking the topology. +On two cards offload is not optional — the expert weights do not fit without it. + +```bash 4 GPUs with DiT layerwise offload +sglang serve \ + --model-path sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview \ + --num-gpus 4 \ + --ulysses-degree 4 \ + --performance-mode memory \ + --dit-layerwise-offload \ + --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ + --port 30010 +``` + +`--dit-layerwise-offload` streams DiT blocks with asynchronous host-to-device +prefetch overlap and selects only the DiT layerwise group. Measured at 896x512 +over 20 steps, it moves peak from 96202 MiB to 83594 MiB and costs 1.5 s — 13% of +peak memory for 1.2% of latency, because the prefetch overlaps transfers with +compute. This is the lever to reach for first. + +Raise `--dit-layerwise-resident-layers` to pin leading blocks on GPU across +denoise steps when VRAM allows; resident layers are transferred once instead of +being re-streamed every step, which trades memory for latency more efficiently +than raising the prefetch size. + +`--cpu-offload-components dit` did not reduce peak on the same measurement (96202 +MiB either way): the DiT has to be resident through denoise, so whole-component +offload has nothing to move. `--performance-mode memory` likewise lands within a +couple of percent of `speed` on both time and peak. Neither is a substitute for +the layerwise flag here. + +The Qwen3.5 text encoder is 52 GiB and stays on the host regardless of these +flags, and its forward runs there too. Staging it onto a card costs 42-84 s for a +3 s GPU forward against 24 s on the CPU, and the transfer spikes 52 GiB on top of +the resident DiTs, which is enough to fail the second request of a run. Only one +rank encodes; the embedding is broadcast to the others. + + +Set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` when running the +two-stage 1080p tier. Both DiTs stay resident through decode, and the 1080p +window decode requests a single ~9 GiB block; without expandable segments that +allocation fails on fragmentation while tens of GiB sit reserved but unallocated. + + + +DiT layerwise offload and cache-dit are mutually exclusive. With +`SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED` set and DiT selected for layerwise offload, SGLang +raises rather than running: cache-dit may reuse a skipped block whose weights +layerwise offload has already released, which surfaces as a shape mismatch. +Disable `--dit-layerwise-offload`, remove `dit` from +`--layerwise-offload-components`, or unset `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED`. DiT +layerwise offload also disables FSDP inference, with a warning rather than an +error. + + +## 7. Configuration notes + +- Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted. The tier is selected by the + requested geometry, not by a separate flag. +- The clip length is fixed at 10 seconds. `num_frames` and `fps` must agree with + that duration to within one frame, which is why the default is 249 frames at + 25 fps rather than a round 250. +- 249 is `(63 - 1) * 4 + 1`. The refiner latent has 63 frames and the turbo + decoder is causal, so the first latent yields one frame and each later one + yields four. +- Video and audio carry separate guidance scales, and the refiner carries its own + pair. The request defaults are 5.0 and 7.0 for the preview pass, and 2.0 and + 5.0 for the refiner. These are request fields, not CLI flags; + `--guidance-scale` sets the video scale only. +- `--num-inference-steps` defaults to 100 for the preview pass. Neither DiT is + step-distilled, so this dominates wall-clock time. The refiner runs 5 steps. +- The refiner, the expert-parallel degree, and the distilled turbo decoder are + pipeline-configuration fields (`enable_refiner`, `ep_size`, `use_turbo_vae`) + with no dedicated CLI flags. Set them by passing a JSON file to + `--pipeline-config-path`, for example `{"ep_size": 4}` for the 8-card launch. + Turning off `use_turbo_vae` falls back to the video VAE decode path and is a + configuration-only change. +- Audio is delivered as stereo at 44100 Hz. +@dataclass
+class Magi2PipelineConfig(PipelineConfig):
+    """MAGI-2-preview: joint audio-video generation from one MoE checkpoint.
+
+    A 40-layer MoE preview DiT and a 30-layer dense refiner DiT share the root
+    checkpoint; the refiner is only reachable at 1080p.
+    """
+
+    task_type: ModelTaskType = ModelTaskType.TI2V
+
+    # ref_image_type is "original", so the generic TI2V resize/centre-crop must not run.
+    skip_input_image_preprocess: bool = True
+
+    # No model_index.json, so nothing loads through sglang's diffusers loaders.
+    native_only_components: tuple[str, ...] = (
+        "text_encoder",
+        "tokenizer",
+        "transformer",
+        "transformer_2",
+        "vae",
+        "turbo_vae",
+        "audio_vae",
+    )
+
+    dit_config: Magi2PreviewConfig = field(default_factory=Magi2PreviewConfig)
+    refiner_dit_config: Magi2RefinerConfig = field(default_factory=Magi2RefinerConfig)
+    dit_precision: str = "bf16"
+
+    vae_config: Magi2VideoVAEConfig = field(default_factory=Magi2VideoVAEConfig)
+    vae_precision: str = "fp32"
+    turbo_vae_config: Magi2TurboVAEConfig = field(default_factory=Magi2TurboVAEConfig)
+    audio_vae_config: Magi2AudioVAEConfig = field(default_factory=Magi2AudioVAEConfig)
+    audio_vae_precision: str = "fp32"
+
+    text_encoder_configs: tuple[Magi2TextEncoderConfig, ...] = field(
+        default_factory=lambda: (Magi2TextEncoderConfig(),)
+    )
+    text_encoder_precisions: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=lambda: ("bf16",))
+    text_encoder_extra_args: list[dict] = field(default_factory=lambda: [{}])
+
+    should_use_guidance: bool = True
+    flow_shift: float | None = 7.0
+    refiner_flow_shift: float = 5.0
+
+    enable_refiner: bool = True
+
+    # Index into the ZeroSNR discretization used to renoise the upsampled preview.
+    refiner_renoise_index: int = 220
+
+    use_turbo_vae: bool = True
+
+    output_audio_sample_rate: int | None = 44100
+    output_audio_channels: int | None = 2
+
+    # Defaults to world size and must divide moe_num_heads (12), so 8 ranks need an
+    # explicit ep_size of 4: two expert-parallel groups, each holding all 12 heads.
+    ep_size: int | None = None
+
+    def get_model_deployment_config(self) -> ModelDeploymentConfig:
+        return ModelDeploymentConfig(
+            supports_cfg_parallel=False,
+            auto_enable_cfg_parallel=False,
+            keep_resident_components=("vae", "turbo_vae", "audio_vae"),
+        )
+
+    def supports_disaggregation(self) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    def _warn_about_allocator(self) -> None:
+        """Warn at startup when the allocator will fail the 1080p decode."""
+        if not self.enable_refiner:
+            return
+        conf = os.environ.get("PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF", "")
+        if "expandable_segments:True" in conf:
+            return
+        logger.warning(
+            "[magi2] PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF does not enable expandable_segments "
+            "(currently %r). The two-stage 1080p tier requests a single ~9 GiB "
+            "block during decode while both DiTs are resident, which typically "
+            "fails on fragmentation after several minutes of denoising. Set "
+            "PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True before launching, "
+            "or run the preview-only tier.",
+            conf or "unset",
+        )
+
+    def validate_server_args(self, server_args) -> None:
+        super().validate_server_args(server_args)
+        self._warn_about_allocator()
+
+        if server_args.enable_cfg_parallel:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MAGI-2's denoise loop runs both CFG branches itself; "
+                "--enable-cfg-parallel would double-apply the guidance"
+            )
+
+        if server_args.attention_backend not in (None, "fa"):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MAGI-2's preview DiT needs FlashAttention for its per-head sink "
+                f"logits; --attention-backend {server_args.attention_backend!r} "
+                "would drop them. Use --attention-backend fa or leave it unset."
+            )
+
+        if server_args.dp_size > 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MAGI-2 builds its expert-parallel groups and head checks over the "
+                f"global world, which spans data-parallel replicas; --dp-size "
+                f"({server_args.dp_size}) must be 1"
+            )
+
+        if server_args.tp_size > 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MAGI-2 has no tensor-parallel layers; --tp-size "
+                f"({server_args.tp_size}) would leave those ranks duplicating "
+                "work instead of sharding the sequence (measured 1.7x slower at "
+                "tp=2, 4.9x at tp=4). Put the whole degree in --ulysses-degree."
+            )
+
+        if server_args.ring_degree > 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MAGI-2 shards its packed sequence over the full SP group but "
+                "exchanges attention heads over the Ulysses group only; "
+                f"--ring-degree ({server_args.ring_degree}) must be 1. Put the "
+                "whole degree in --ulysses-degree."
+            )
+
+        num_gpus = server_args.num_gpus
+        ep_size = self.ep_size or num_gpus
+        if num_gpus % ep_size:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"num_gpus ({num_gpus}) must be divisible by ep_size ({ep_size})"
+            )
+
+        moe_heads = self.dit_config.arch_config.moe_num_heads
+        if moe_heads % ep_size:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MAGI-2 splits {moe_heads} MoE heads across expert-parallel "
+                f"ranks; ep_size ({ep_size}) must divide {moe_heads}"
+            )
+
+        # Ulysses axes only. The MoE head axis is checked against ep_size above,
+        # which is what shards it; ep_size may be smaller than num_gpus.
+        preview = self.dit_config.arch_config
+        axes = {"preview attention heads": preview.num_attention_heads}
+        if self.enable_refiner:
+            refiner = self.refiner_dit_config.arch_config
+            axes["refiner attention heads"] = refiner.num_attention_heads
+            axes["refiner KV heads"] = refiner.num_query_groups
+
+        for name, count in sorted(axes.items(), key=lambda item: item[1]):
+            if count % num_gpus:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"MAGI-2 shards {name} ({count}) across ranks; num_gpus "
+                    f"({num_gpus}) must divide it. Valid counts are "
+                    f"{[n for n in range(1, max(axes.values()) + 1) if all(c % n == 0 for c in axes.values())]}"
+                )
+
+
+def register():
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.sample.magi2 import Magi2SamplingParams
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.registry import register_configs
+
+    register_configs(
+        sampling_param_cls=Magi2SamplingParams,
+        pipeline_config_cls=Magi2PipelineConfig,
+        hf_model_paths=["sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview"],
+        model_detectors=[
+            lambda model_id: (
+                "magi-2-preview" in model_id.lower()
+                or "magi2-preview" in model_id.lower()
+            )
+        ],
+    )

+@dataclass
+class Magi2SamplingParams(SamplingParams):
+    """Request parameters for MAGI-2-preview; defaults are the shipped two-stage
+    1080p tier (896x512 preview, 1920x1088 refiner)."""
+
+    _default_width: ClassVar[int | None] = 1920
+    _default_height: ClassVar[int | None] = 1088
+    # Fixed-length clips at two fixed sizes: a halved probe fails _validate.
+    supports_warmup_lightening: ClassVar[bool] = False
+
+    negative_prompt: str = MAGI2_NEGATIVE_PROMPT
+
+    num_inference_steps: int = 100
+    refiner_num_inference_steps: int = 5
+
+    preview_width: int = 896
+    preview_height: int = 512
+
+    num_frames: int = MAGI2_NUM_FRAMES
+    fps: int = MAGI2_REFINER_FPS
+
+    guidance_scale: float = 5.0
+    audio_guidance_scale: float = 7.0
+    refiner_guidance_scale: float = 2.0
+    refiner_audio_guidance_scale: float = 5.0
+
+    use_skimmed_guidance: bool = False
+    skimmed_guidance_scale: float = 3.0
+
+    generate_audio: bool = True
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if self.supported_resolutions is None:
+            self.supported_resolutions = list(MAGI2_RESOLUTIONS)
+        super().__post_init__()
+
+    def _validate(self) -> None:
+        super()._validate()
+
+        if (self.width, self.height) not in MAGI2_RESOLUTIONS:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MAGI-2 supports {MAGI2_RESOLUTIONS}, got {self.width}x{self.height}"
+            )
+
+        # Tolerance: causal decode yields 4k+1 frames, and num_frames is rounded up
+        # so the latent count divides the sequence-parallel degree.
+        nominal_frames = MAGI2_CLIP_SECONDS * self.fps
+        if abs(self.num_frames - nominal_frames) > 0.05 * nominal_frames:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MAGI-2 only generates {MAGI2_CLIP_SECONDS:g}s clips, i.e. "
+                f"about {round(nominal_frames)} frames at fps={self.fps}; got "
+                f"{self.num_frames}"
+            )
+
+        if self.num_inference_steps is not None and self.num_inference_steps < 1:
+            raise ValueError("num_inference_steps must be >= 1")
+        if self.refiner_num_inference_steps < 1:
+            raise ValueError("refiner_num_inference_steps must be >= 1")
+
+    def prepare_synthetic_warmup_request_for_queue(
+        self, req: Any, server_args: Any
+    ) -> None:
+        # The generic default picks the 896x512 preview-only tier, which never
+        # runs the refiner or the 1080p decode.
+        if server_args.warmup_resolutions is not None:
+            return
+        req.width, req.height = self._default_width, self._default_height
+        if server_args.warmup_num_frames is not None:
+            return
+        # Warmup skips _adjust, so apply the same per-GPU rounding real requests get.
+        req.num_frames = (
+            align_num_frames_for_num_gpus(
+                MAGI2_NUM_FRAMES,
+                num_gpus=server_args.num_gpus,
+                vae_config=server_args.pipeline_config.vae_config,
+                round_down=self.num_frames_round_down,
+            )
+            if self.adjust_frames
+            else MAGI2_NUM_FRAMES
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def lower_video_request_kwargs(
+        cls,
+        request: Any,
+        kwargs: dict[str, Any],
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        # The video API synthesizes num_frames as fps * seconds from its own 24fps
+        # 4s defaults, which a fixed-length 10s model rejects. Drop both unless the
+        # caller set them, so this type's 249 @ 25 applies.
+        kwargs = dict(kwargs)
+        if request.fps is None:
+            kwargs.pop("fps", None)
+        if request.num_frames is None:
+            kwargs.pop("num_frames", None)
+        return kwargs

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+import math
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from torch import nn
+from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import BlockMask, create_mask, flex_attention
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.dits.magi2 import Magi2RefinerArchConfig
+
+_TILE = 128
+
+# Each distinct sequence length compiles its own graph, hence SEQ_BUCKET.
+_flex_attention = torch.compile(flex_attention, dynamic=False)
+
+try:
+    from magi_attention.api import flex_flash_attn_func
+
+    _HAS_FFA = True
+except ImportError:
+    # Optional: the flex path below is equivalent, just 2.5x slower here.
+    flex_flash_attn_func = None
+    _HAS_FFA = False
+
+
+class Magi2BlockGrid(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """Frozen so it can key the mask cache."""
+
+    latent_thw: tuple[int, int, int]
+    block_thw: tuple[int, int, int]
+    radius_thw: tuple[int, int, int]
+    num_tail_tokens: int
+    num_pad_tokens: int = 0
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_arch_config(
+        cls,
+        *,
+        arch_config: Magi2RefinerArchConfig,
+        latent_thw: tuple[int, int, int],
+        num_tail_tokens: int,
+        num_pad_tokens: int = 0,
+    ) -> Magi2BlockGrid:
+        return cls(
+            latent_thw=latent_thw,
+            block_thw=(
+                arch_config.block_t_size,
+                arch_config.block_size,
+                arch_config.block_size,
+            ),
+            radius_thw=(
+                arch_config.block_t_radius,
+                arch_config.block_h_radius,
+                arch_config.block_w_radius,
+            ),
+            num_tail_tokens=num_tail_tokens,
+            num_pad_tokens=num_pad_tokens,
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def num_video_tokens(self) -> int:
+        return math.prod(self.latent_thw)
+
+    @property
+    def num_valid_tokens(self) -> int:
+        return self.num_video_tokens + self.num_tail_tokens
+
+    @property
+    def seq_len(self) -> int:
+        return self.num_valid_tokens + self.num_pad_tokens
+
+    @property
+    def block_grid_thw(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+        t, h, w = (math.ceil(n / b) for n, b in zip(self.latent_thw, self.block_thw))
+        return (t, h, w)
+
+    @property
+    def num_tiles(self) -> int:
+        return math.ceil(self.seq_len / _TILE)
+
+
+# Divides every supported sp degree, so the shard adds no padding of its own.
+SEQ_BUCKET = 8 * _TILE
+
+
+def _dim_block_sizes(*, dim: int, block: int, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    sizes = torch.full(
+        (math.ceil(dim / block),), block, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+    )
+    sizes[-1] = dim - block * (sizes.numel() - 1)
+    return sizes
+
+
+def _block_token_counts(*, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    t_sizes, h_sizes, w_sizes = (
+        _dim_block_sizes(dim=dim, block=block, device=device)
+        for dim, block in zip(grid.latent_thw, grid.block_thw)
+    )
+    return (
+        t_sizes[:, None, None] * h_sizes[None, :, None] * w_sizes[None, None, :]
+    ).flatten()
+
+
+def block_scan_order(
+    *, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    nt, nh, nw = grid.block_grid_thw
+    bt, bh, bw = grid.block_thw
+    ids = torch.arange(grid.num_video_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    padded = ids.new_full((nt * bt, nh * bh, nw * bw), -1)
+    t, h, w = grid.latent_thw
+    padded[:t, :h, :w] = ids.view(t, h, w)
+    scan = padded.view(nt, bt, nh, bh, nw, bw).permute(0, 2, 4, 1, 3, 5).reshape(-1)
+    tail = torch.arange(
+        grid.num_video_tokens, grid.seq_len, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+    )
+    order = torch.cat([scan[scan >= 0], tail])
+    restore = torch.empty_like(order)
+    restore[order] = torch.arange(order.numel(), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    return order, restore
+
+
+def _token_block_coords(
+    *, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Must cover the padded length: the kernel evaluates ``mask_mod`` on the full tile including its ragged end."""
+    counts = _block_token_counts(grid=grid, device=device)
+    ids = torch.repeat_interleave(
+        torch.arange(counts.numel(), dtype=torch.int64, device=device), counts
+    )
+    ids = F.pad(ids, (0, grid.num_tiles * _TILE - grid.num_video_tokens))
+    _, nh, nw = grid.block_grid_thw
+    return (
+        (ids // (nh * nw)).to(torch.int32),
+        (ids // nw % nh).to(torch.int32),
+        (ids % nw).to(torch.int32),
+    )
+
+
+def build_mask_mod(*, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device):
+    # Only video->video is grid-local; the tail attends densely.
+    block_t, block_h, block_w = _token_block_coords(grid=grid, device=device)
+    # dynamo guards a captured int BY VALUE, so the prompt-dependent valid length
+    # must be a tensor; num_video is tier-fixed and safe as an int.
+    num_video = grid.num_video_tokens
+    is_valid_key = (
+        torch.arange(grid.num_tiles * _TILE, device=device) < grid.num_valid_tokens
+    )
+    radius_t, radius_h, radius_w = grid.radius_thw
+
+    def mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
+        video_pair = (q_idx < num_video) & (kv_idx < num_video)
+        near = (
+            ((block_t[q_idx] - block_t[kv_idx]).abs() <= radius_t)
+            & ((block_h[q_idx] - block_h[kv_idx]).abs() <= radius_h)
+            & ((block_w[q_idx] - block_w[kv_idx]).abs() <= radius_w)
+        )
+        # Pad stays attendable as a query: a fully masked row softmaxes to NaN.
+        return (near | ~video_pair) & is_valid_key[kv_idx]
+
+    return mask_mod
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4)
+def cached_ffa_ranges(
+    *, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """``mask_mod`` as (q, k) token-range pairs: 1.4 MB against the BlockMask's 123 MB.
+
+    A block's neighbours along ``w`` are consecutive block ids, so each ``(t, h)``
+    offset collapses to one contiguous key range.
+    """
+    counts = _block_token_counts(grid=grid, device=device)
+    starts = F.pad(counts.cumsum(0), (1, 0)).to(torch.int32)
+    nt, nh, nw = grid.block_grid_thw
+    radius_t, radius_h, radius_w = grid.radius_thw
+
+    ids = torch.arange(nt * nh * nw, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    block_t, block_h, block_w = ids // (nh * nw), ids // nw % nh, ids % nw
+    offs_t = torch.arange(-radius_t, radius_t + 1, device=device)
+    offs_h = torch.arange(-radius_h, radius_h + 1, device=device)
+
+    near_t = block_t[:, None, None] + offs_t[None, :, None]
+    near_h = block_h[:, None, None] + offs_h[None, None, :]
+    inside = (near_t >= 0) & (near_t < nt) & (near_h >= 0) & (near_h < nh)
+    base = (near_t.clamp(0, nt - 1) * nh + near_h.clamp(0, nh - 1)) * nw
+    lo = (block_w - radius_w).clamp(min=0)[:, None, None]
+    hi = (block_w + radius_w).clamp(max=nw - 1)[:, None, None]
+
+    q_lo = starts[ids][:, None, None].expand_as(base)[inside]
+    q_hi = starts[ids + 1][:, None, None].expand_as(base)[inside]
+    q_ranges = [torch.stack((q_lo, q_hi), dim=-1)]
+    k_ranges = [
+        torch.stack((starts[base + lo][inside], starts[base + hi + 1][inside]), dim=-1)
+    ]
+
+    num_video, num_valid = grid.num_video_tokens, grid.num_valid_tokens
+    extra = []
+    if num_valid > num_video:
+        # Only video->video is grid-local, so every video query sees the whole tail.
+        extra.append(((0, num_video), (num_video, num_valid)))
+    if grid.seq_len > num_video:
+        # Tail and pad queries attend densely; a fully masked pad row would be NaN.
+        extra.append(((num_video, grid.seq_len), (0, num_valid)))
+    for (q0, q1), (k0, k1) in extra:
+        q_ranges.append(torch.tensor([[q0, q1]], dtype=torch.int32, device=device))
+        k_ranges.append(torch.tensor([[k0, k1]], dtype=torch.int32, device=device))
+
+    return torch.cat(q_ranges), torch.cat(k_ranges)
+
+
+def _tile_coord_bounds(
+    *, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """``lo``/``hi`` are [3, num_tiles]; a tile with no video token gets ``lo > hi``."""
+    coords = torch.stack(_token_block_coords(grid=grid, device=device))
+    positions = torch.arange(coords.shape[1], dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    is_video = (positions < grid.num_video_tokens).expand(3, -1)
+    unreachable = torch.iinfo(torch.int32).max // 2
+    tiles = (3, grid.num_tiles, _TILE)
+    lo = torch.where(is_video, coords, unreachable).view(tiles).amin(-1)
+    hi = torch.where(is_video, coords, -unreachable).view(tiles).amax(-1)
+    has_tail = (
+        ((positions >= grid.num_video_tokens) & (positions < grid.seq_len))
+        .view(grid.num_tiles, _TILE)
+        .any(-1)
+    )
+    return lo, hi, has_tail
+
+
+def _tile_near(*, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Tile pairs whose video block ranges come within ``radius_thw`` on every axis."""
+    lo, hi, _ = _tile_coord_bounds(grid=grid, device=device)
+    near = torch.ones((grid.num_tiles, grid.num_tiles), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+    for axis, radius in enumerate(grid.radius_thw):
+        near &= (lo[axis][:, None] - radius <= hi[axis][None, :]) & (
+            hi[axis][:, None] + radius >= lo[axis][None, :]
+        )
+    return near
+
+
+def _tile_occupancy(*, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A superset of the true mask, which ``mask_mod`` then masks elementwise."""
+    _, _, has_tail = _tile_coord_bounds(grid=grid, device=device)
+    near = _tile_near(grid=grid, device=device)
+    return near | has_tail[:, None] | has_tail[None, :]
+
+
+def _tile_kinds(
+    *, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Which tiles hold one block of video, only tail, or any pad key."""
+    lo, hi, has_tail = _tile_coord_bounds(grid=grid, device=device)
+    positions = torch.arange(grid.num_tiles * _TILE, device=device)
+    tiled = positions.view(grid.num_tiles, _TILE)
+    has_video = (tiled < grid.num_video_tokens).any(-1)
+    has_pad = (tiled >= grid.num_valid_tokens).any(-1)
+    # lo == hi on every axis means all of the tile's video tokens sit in one block,
+    # which holds for a full block but not for a ragged edge one.
+    single_block = ((lo == hi).all(0)) & has_video
+    return single_block & ~has_tail & ~has_pad, ~has_video & ~has_pad, has_pad
+
+
+def _tile_full(*, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Tile pairs with no masked element, so the kernel can skip ``mask_mod`` on them."""
+    video, tail, has_pad = _tile_kinds(grid=grid, device=device)
+    both_video = video[:, None] & video[None, :] & _tile_near(grid=grid, device=device)
+    # A tail token on either side clears the video-only test for the whole pair.
+    with_tail = (tail[:, None] & (video | tail)[None, :]) | (
+        video[:, None] & tail[None, :]
+    )
+    return (both_video | with_tail) & ~has_pad[None, :]
+
+
+def _rows_to_blockmask_args(keep: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    counts = keep.sum(-1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    # Keep all num_tiles columns rather than trimming to counts.max(): from_kv_blocks
+    # sizes its transposed-mask buffer from kv_indices.shape[-1].
+    indices = keep.to(torch.int8).argsort(dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True)
+    return counts[None, None], indices.to(torch.int32)[None, None].contiguous()
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=2)
+def cached_block_mask(*, grid: Magi2BlockGrid, device: torch.device) -> BlockMask:
+    """Built sparsely because ``create_block_mask`` materializes a dense [seq_len, seq_len] bool first."""
+    allow = _tile_occupancy(grid=grid, device=device)
+    full = _tile_full(grid=grid, device=device) & allow
+    full_counts, full_indices = _rows_to_blockmask_args(full)
+    # Only the ragged and pad-bearing pairs are left to mask elementwise.
+    counts, indices = _rows_to_blockmask_args(allow & ~full)
+    return BlockMask.from_kv_blocks(
+        kv_num_blocks=counts,
+        kv_indices=indices,
+        full_kv_num_blocks=full_counts,
+        full_kv_indices=full_indices,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=(_TILE, _TILE),
+        mask_mod=build_mask_mod(grid=grid, device=device),
+        seq_lengths=(grid.seq_len, grid.seq_len),
+    )
+
+
+class Magi2BlockGridAttention(nn.Module):
+    """Q/K/V must already be in ``block_scan_order``; only video->video is grid-local."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        num_heads: int,
+        head_dim: int,
+        num_kv_heads: int | None = None,
+        softmax_scale: float | None = None,
+        dense_fallback: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads = num_heads
+        self.head_dim = head_dim
+        self.num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads or num_heads
+        self.softmax_scale = softmax_scale or head_dim**-0.5
+        self.enable_gqa = self.num_kv_heads != num_heads
+        self.dense_fallback = dense_fallback
+
+    # Opaque to dynamo: the mask is compiled by _flex_attention above, and an outer
+    # region would recompile it per sequence length instead of per bucket.
+    @torch._dynamo.disable()
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        grid: Magi2BlockGrid,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.distributed.parallel_state import (
+            get_ulysses_parallel_world_size,
+        )
+        from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.usp import (
+            _usp_input_all_to_all,
+            _usp_output_all_to_all,
+        )
+
+        ulysses = get_ulysses_parallel_world_size() > 1
+        if ulysses:
+            # Per-tensor: the packed helper asserts q/k/v share a shape, and this is GQA.
+            q, k, v = (_usp_input_all_to_all(t[None], head_dim=2)[0] for t in (q, k, v))
+
+        if _HAS_FFA and not self.dense_fallback:
+            # FFA takes the packed [S, H, D] layout directly, with no transpose.
+            out = self._attend_ffa(q=q, k=k, v=v, grid=grid)
+        else:
+            out = self._attend(
+                q=q.transpose(0, 1)[None],
+                k=k.transpose(0, 1)[None],
+                v=v.transpose(0, 1)[None],
+                grid=grid,
+            )[0].transpose(0, 1)
+
+        if ulysses:
+            out = _usp_output_all_to_all(out[None], head_dim=2)[0]
+        return out
+
+    def _attend_ffa(
+        self,
+        *,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        grid: Magi2BlockGrid,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        q_ranges, k_ranges = cached_ffa_ranges(grid=grid, device=q.device)
+        out, _ = flex_flash_attn_func(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            q_ranges,
+            k_ranges,
+            softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale,
+            # Measured free (41.99 vs 41.06 ms) and keeps runs reproducible.
+            deterministic=True,
+            disable_fwd_atomic_reduction=True,
+            auto_range_merge=True,
+        )
+        return out
+
+    def _attend(
+        self,
+        *,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        grid: Magi2BlockGrid,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self.dense_fallback:
+            mask = create_mask(
+                build_mask_mod(grid=grid, device=q.device),
+                1,
+                1,
+                grid.seq_len,
+                grid.seq_len,
+                device=q.device,
+            )
+            return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+                q,
+                k,
+                v,
+                attn_mask=mask,
+                scale=self.softmax_scale,
+                enable_gqa=self.enable_gqa,
+            )
+        return _flex_attention(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            block_mask=cached_block_mask(grid=grid, device=q.device),
+            scale=self.softmax_scale,
+            enable_gqa=self.enable_gqa,
+        )

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.distributed.parallel_state import (
+    get_ulysses_parallel_rank,
+    get_ulysses_parallel_world_size,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends.attention_backend import (
+    AttentionRequirements,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends.flash_attn import (
+    FlashAttentionImpl,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.selector import get_attn_backend
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import AttentionBackendEnum
+
+
+class Magi2SinkAttention(nn.Module):
+    """``USPAttention``'s varlen paths cannot pass sink logits, so this drives ``FlashAttentionImpl`` directly."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        num_heads: int,
+        head_dim: int,
+        num_kv_heads: int | None = None,
+        softmax_scale: float | None = None,
+        sink_token_num: int = 0,
+        window_size: tuple[int, int] = (-1, -1),
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads = num_heads
+        self.head_dim = head_dim
+        self.num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads or num_heads
+        self.softmax_scale = softmax_scale or head_dim**-0.5
+        self.window_size = window_size
+
+        # fp32: compared against attention logits, and the reference avoids bf16 here.
+        self.sinks = (
+            nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(sink_token_num, num_heads, dtype=torch.float32))
+            if sink_token_num
+            else None
+        )
+        self._impl = None
+
+    def _local_sinks(self) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+        """``_usp_input_all_to_all_packed_qkv`` gives rank *r* heads ``[r * h_local, (r + 1) * h_local)``."""
+        if self.sinks is None:
+            return None
+        if self.sinks.shape[0] != 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "FlashAttention takes one sink logit per head, so "
+                f"sink_token_num must be 1; got {self.sinks.shape[0]}"
+            )
+        # The checkpoint stores [sink_token_num, num_heads]; the kernel wants flat.
+        sinks = self.sinks[0]
+        world_size = get_ulysses_parallel_world_size()
+        if world_size <= 1:
+            return sinks
+        h_local = self.num_heads // world_size
+        start = get_ulysses_parallel_rank() * h_local
+        return sinks[start : start + h_local]
+
+    def _ensure_impl(self, dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+        if self._impl is not None:
+            return
+        backend = get_attn_backend(
+            self.head_dim,
+            dtype,
+            supported_attention_backends={AttentionBackendEnum.FA},
+            selected_attention_backend=AttentionBackendEnum.FA,
+            attention_requirements=AttentionRequirements(packed_varlen=True),
+        )
+        impl_cls = backend.get_impl_cls()
+        # The platform FA resolver can still hand back SDPA, which drops sinks.
+        if not issubclass(impl_cls, FlashAttentionImpl):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "MAGI-2 attention needs FlashAttention for its sink logits and "
+                f"window, but the platform resolved {backend.get_enum().name}; "
+                "run on a GPU with FA support"
+            )
+        world_size = get_ulysses_parallel_world_size()
+        local_heads = self.num_heads // world_size
+        local_kv_heads = max(1, self.num_kv_heads // world_size)
+        sinks = self._local_sinks()
+        self._impl = impl_cls(
+            num_heads=local_heads,
+            head_size=self.head_dim,
+            causal=False,
+            softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale,
+            num_kv_heads=local_kv_heads,
+            # The parameter stays fp32, but FA3 wants sinks in the q dtype.
+            sinks=None if sinks is None else sinks.to(dtype).contiguous(),
+            window_size=self.window_size,
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+        max_seqlen: int,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.usp import (
+            _usp_input_all_to_all_packed_qkv,
+            _usp_output_all_to_all,
+        )
+
+        ulysses = get_ulysses_parallel_world_size() > 1
+        if ulysses:
+            q, k, v = _usp_input_all_to_all_packed_qkv(q, k, v)
+
+        self._ensure_impl(q.dtype)
+        out = self._impl.forward_varlen(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+            max_seqlen=max_seqlen,
+        )
+
+        if ulysses:
+            out = _usp_output_all_to_all(out[None], head_dim=2)[0]
+        return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
